facts: Clarke County Board of Supervisors passed Resolution #25-011 establishing a temporary moratorium on construction of data centers in unincorporated areas of Clarke County, Iowa
The moratorium remains in place until the Board passes a permanent moratorium, passes a regulating ordinance, or rescinds it
The moratorium resolution passed 3-0 with Randy Dunbar, Dean Robins and Brian Sorensen voting aye

facts: Donna Juber presented the Hardin County Board of Supervisors with a potential resolution to impose a two-year moratorium on building data centers in Hardin County.
Juber said half of Iowa's counties have placed moratoriums on data centers.
On Sept. 3, the Hardin County Zoning Commission voted unanimously not to recommend changes to ordinances prohibiting a battery energy storage system near Radcliffe.
NextEra's Garden Wind Energy Project began operations in 2009 with 100 turbines, 77 of them in Hardin County.

quotes.text: “We would approach it from the standpoint that we’re considering zoning,” said McMeen.
“I think our intent is to do an ordinance down the road,” said Supervisor Abigail Maas.

facts: Iowa County is preparing to pass a moratorium on building data centers, as many other counties in the state have
County Attorney Tim McMeen suggested a 12-month moratorium to study possible requirements for the facilities
Iowa County does not have zoning ordinances, and the county has not had any requests for data centers

news.title: Google data center near Palo would use 10.4M gallons of water per day | Environmental News, Nature News | thegazette.com

quotes.text: There is no influence from Google in the study itself.
At every Google site, we conduct a rigorous, multifactor watershed health assessment.
quotes.source: Kiran Udayakumar, technical program manager for utility infrastructure strategy and planning at Google

facts: Google's proposed Palo data center could use up to 10.4 million gallons of water per day from the Cedar River
Google's assessment estimates 2.3 million gallons returned to the river and 8.1 million lost to evaporation daily
Linn County approved an agreement with Google for an independent water balance study, due March 2027
The site is in unincorporated Linn County and Google intends to seek annexation into Palo city limits
